title: A Concise History of the Castle and the Newcastles
source: Transcribed from The Park Map, Fourth Edition, designed by Dougal de Havilland and donated to the Nottingham Park Residents' Association.
note: Extracted from the PDF's own text layer, so the wording is his. Long entries are truncated where the map's column wrapped — worth checking against the original before publishing.

entries.text: Saxons arrive, ignore the Castle rock and build their settlement where St Mary's church and the Lace Market now stand.
William the Conqueror sees the rock and orders a castle to be built there by his son Peverel. Adjacent woodland is enclosed
A Great Charter is granted to Nottingham, and the town is now subservient only to the King
Richard III allegedly musters his troops in the Deer Park and marches them across The King's Meadow and on to Bosworth.
Charles I chooses to stay at Thurland Hall, the castle having become "unsuitable"

The ruined castle is bought by William Cavendish who will be created 1st Duke of Newcastle in 1665 for his Civil War royal support.
Work begins on this Italianate palace costing £14,000 but the Duke dies before it is finished.
